items.prompt: Which structure belongs to the peripheral nervous system?

choices.c: A spinal nerve carrying sensory and motor axons

items.rationale: Nerves outside the brain and spinal cord belong to the peripheral nervous system; the brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system.

targetedFeedback.a: The spinal cord is part of the central nervous system.
targetedFeedback.b: The cerebral cortex is brain tissue and therefore central nervous system.
targetedFeedback.d: The brainstem is part of the brain and central nervous system.

items.prompt: A person understands spoken words and can write a reply, but speech production is slow and effortful. Which evidence-based inference is strongest?

choices.a: A language-production network may be affected while comprehension networks remain more functional.
choices.b: The person must be left-brained and creative.
choices.c: The spinal cord is the only possible site of disruption.
choices.d: One symptom proves a complete diagnosis.

items.rationale: The contrast between relatively preserved comprehension and disrupted speech production can help localize a functional network, while remaining insufficient for diagnosis.

targetedFeedback.b: Left-brain/right-brain personality categories are a neuromyth and do not explain this pattern.
targetedFeedback.c: The pattern concerns language processing, which depends strongly on distributed brain networks.
targetedFeedback.d: Localization is an evidence-based hypothesis; diagnosis requires broader clinical evidence.

items.prompt: Which finding would most weaken the claim that complex thinking occurs in one isolated brain centre?

choices.a: Several connected regions change activity as a learner plans and evaluates a response.

items.rationale: Coordinated activity across connected regions directly supports a network explanation of complex cognition.

targetedFeedback.b: Two hemispheres alone do not show how complex processing is distributed.
targetedFeedback.c: A structural label does not provide functional evidence about complex thinking.
targetedFeedback.d: Reflex speed concerns a different pathway and does not test the isolated-centre claim.

items.prompt: Which sequence correctly represents a basic withdrawal reflex arc?

choices.a: Effector → motor neuron → receptor → sensory neuron
choices.b: Receptor → sensory neuron → central integration → motor neuron → effector

items.rationale: A receptor detects the stimulus, sensory input enters the CNS, central synapses organize output, and a motor neuron carries the response to an effector.

targetedFeedback.a: This reverses the information flow and begins with the effector.
targetedFeedback.c: A withdrawal reflex does not require a hormone route and begins with receptor input.
targetedFeedback.d: The receptor and sensory neuron must occur before motor output.

items.prompt: In a ruler-drop investigation, which change best improves reliability without changing the research question?

choices.a: Use several trials per condition and compare median response distance.
choices.b: Tell the participant exactly when the ruler will drop.
choices.c: Use a different participant and ruler on every trial.
choices.d: Discard every slow result after seeing the data.

items.rationale: Repeated trials reduce the influence of random variation, and a median limits the effect of an unusual trial while preserving the question.

targetedFeedback.b: Predictable timing changes the task by adding anticipation.
targetedFeedback.c: Changing multiple factors makes condition comparisons harder to interpret.
targetedFeedback.d: Removing results after inspection introduces bias unless a rule was defined in advance.

items.prompt: Condition A has a median response distance of 18 cm and Condition B has 17 cm, with both ranging from 8–31 cm. What conclusion is best supported?

choices.a: Condition B is conclusively faster for all people.
choices.b: The medians differ slightly, but overlap and variability make a strong causal claim unwarranted.
choices.c: The nervous system was inactive in Condition A.
choices.d: The extreme values should automatically be deleted.

items.rationale: A one-centimetre median difference is small relative to the broad overlapping ranges, so the result supports caution and more evidence.

targetedFeedback.a: The overlapping values do not support a universal or conclusive claim.
targetedFeedback.c: A recorded response shows the nervous system was active; the data concern timing variability.
targetedFeedback.d: Extreme values require a pre-defined, evidence-based exclusion rule rather than automatic removal.
